pack.name: Monitoring
pack.description: Watch what matters — health checks, webhooks, disk reports, and status pings on a schedule.

templates.name: Log Disk Usage
templates.description: Append free/used disk space for every drive to a log file.
templates.commandTemplate: powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command "Get-PSDrive -PSProvider FileSystem | Select-Object Name, Used, Free | Out-File -Append '{{logPath}}'"

parameters.label: Log file path
parameters.help: Where to append the disk snapshot.

templates.name: Ping Host & Log
templates.description: Check whether a host is reachable and append the result to a log.

parameters.label: Host / IP
parameters.help: The hostname or IP to ping.

parameters.label: Log file path
parameters.help: Where to append the ping result.

templates.name: Log Service Status
templates.description: Record whether a Windows service is running, on an interval.

parameters.label: Service name
parameters.help: The service short name to check.

parameters.label: Log file path
parameters.help: Where to append the status.

templates.name: Scan a Log for Errors
templates.description: Search a log file for a pattern and fail the run when it matches, so a job that writes its problems to a file instead of alerting you still turns into something you can see. Supply the log to read and the text or regular expression that counts as trouble.

parameters.label: Log file path
parameters.help: The file to search. A wildcard such as C:\logs\*.log reads every matching file.

parameters.label: Pattern that means trouble
parameters.help: Text or a regular expression. A match exits non-zero, which Cronsole records as a failed run. Avoid single quotes (they close the PowerShell string).

templates.name: Report Failed Scheduled Tasks
templates.description: Append every Windows scheduled task whose last run reported a non-zero result to a report file, so a task that has been failing quietly for a week shows up somewhere you read. Supply the file to append the report to.
templates.commandTemplate: powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command "Get-ScheduledTask | Get-ScheduledTaskInfo | Where-Object LastTaskResult -ne 0 | Format-Table TaskName, LastRunTime, LastTaskResult | Out-File -Append '{{reportPath}}'"

parameters.label: Report file path
parameters.help: Where to append the list of failing tasks. Reading every task needs the run to be elevated on most machines.

templates.name: Log Top Processes by CPU
templates.description: Append the highest CPU-consuming processes to a log file on an interval, so a machine that suddenly runs hot has a paper trail of what was busy.
templates.commandTemplate: powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command "Get-Process | Sort-Object CPU -Descending | Select-Object -First {{topN}} Name, CPU, WorkingSet | Format-Table -AutoSize | Out-File -Append '{{logPath}}'"

parameters.label: Number of processes
parameters.help: How many top CPU-consuming processes to record.

parameters.label: Log file path
parameters.help: Where to append the process snapshot.

templates.name: Log Physical Disk Health (Windows)
templates.description: Append each physical disk’s health and operational status to a log file on a schedule, so a drive that starts reporting Warning or Unhealthy leaves a record before it fails outright.
templates.commandTemplate: powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command "Get-PhysicalDisk | Select-Object FriendlyName, MediaType, HealthStatus, OperationalStatus | Format-Table -AutoSize | Out-File -Append '{{logPath}}'"

parameters.label: Log file path
parameters.help: Where to append the disk health snapshot. This reports what Windows already knows about each drive; it is not a full SMART analysis.

templates.name: Log Latest Time Machine Backup (macOS)
templates.description: Write the location of the most recent Time Machine backup to a log file on a schedule, so a backup disk that quietly stopped being written to shows up as a stale entry instead of going unnoticed.

parameters.label: Log file path
parameters.help: Where to append the latest backup path. The command fails when no backup exists or the disk is not mounted, which is the signal worth noticing. The job may need Full Disk Access.

templates.name: Check DNS Resolution & Log
templates.description: Resolve a hostname through the machine DNS resolver and append the answer to a log on a schedule. The task fails when the name does not resolve, so a broken resolver or an expired domain shows up as a failed run instead of a mystery later.

parameters.label: Hostname
parameters.help: The domain name to resolve, for example example.com. Use one you depend on, such as your own site or API host.

parameters.label: Log file path
parameters.help: Where to append each successful answer.

templates.name: Healthchecks.io Status Check (Cronsole)
templates.description: Read a Healthchecks.io status badge and fail the run unless every check behind it is up — a second, independent reader for a cron fleet that runs somewhere else, so a silent outage shows up in Cronsole instead of waiting on an alert email.

parameters.label: Badge JSON URL
parameters.help: From Healthchecks.io › Badges, the JSON format — e.g. https://healthchecks.io/badge/<key>/<tag>.json. A tag badge covers every check with that tag; "*" covers the whole project. A check that is late (grace) fails this too.

templates.name: Published Content Freshness Check (Cronsole)
templates.description: Fail the run when a published page or file has not changed recently, read from its Last-Modified header. The dead-man switch for a generator that stops producing without erroring — the site stays up, so an uptime check stays green.

parameters.label: URL
parameters.help: A page or file the job regenerates — a feed, a sitemap, an index. Must send a Last-Modified header (GitHub Pages and most static hosts do).

parameters.label: Fail when older than (hours)
parameters.help: Set a little above the generator's own cadence: 36 for a daily job, 192 for a weekly one.

templates.name: Domain Expiry Check (Cronsole)
templates.description: Look a domain up over RDAP and fail the run when its registration expires within your warning window. No API key; complements the SSL expiry check, which cannot see a domain that lapses with a valid certificate.

parameters.label: Domain
parameters.help: The registered domain, without a subdomain — e.g. example.com.

parameters.label: Warn within (days)
parameters.help: Fail the run when fewer than this many days remain before the registration expires.

templates.name: Docker Compose Self-Heal
templates.description: Re-run docker compose up on an interval so a dev stack restarts itself if it stops (the pattern Cronsole uses for its own stack).

parameters.label: Compose file path
parameters.help: Absolute path to the docker-compose.yml. up -d is idempotent — running containers are left alone.

templates.name: Webhook / HTTP Ping (Windows)
templates.description: Call a URL on a schedule using Invoke-WebRequest.

parameters.label: URL
parameters.help: The endpoint to call.

parameters.label: HTTP method
parameters.help: HTTP verb for the request.

templates.name: Webhook / HTTP Ping (macOS)
templates.description: Call a URL on a schedule using curl.

parameters.label: HTTP method
parameters.help: HTTP verb for the request.

parameters.label: URL
parameters.help: The endpoint to call.
